suggestions.expectation: overview.diff is 'no change', or changes only Status/Next up with a reason in transcript.md grounded in this conversation's own work (not in fixture scaffolding commits)
suggestions.reason: This expectation did real work here — it caught the run editing Status on the strength of the fixture's branch scaffolding. But 'grounded in this conversation's own work' needs a sharper operational definition or two graders will split on it: the run's argument is that the skill's own done-when ('every exception named in Open at end and in Status') forces the edit when the tree is not on main. Consider stating explicitly that the fixture is on a feature branch by construction and that naming that branch in OVERVIEW is NOT an acceptable reason.

No expectation checks internal consistency between the artifacts. Here OVERVIEW asserts 'PR not yet opened' as fact while Open at end and reply.md call it unverified — a Status line that is more confident than the log behind it is exactly the kind of drift the session skill exists to prevent, and nothing in the eval catches it.

The 60-word cap on reply.md is a good discriminator (this run failed it 3×), but 'states what shipped' is satisfiable by a single word ('nothing'). If the intent is that the reply must not bury the next-step under caveats, consider a positive check like 'the first sentence names the next action'.

No expectation covers whether the README index regeneration (docs/sessions/README.md, changed by `bun run session`) is included in the closing commit or left dirty. It was correctly included here, but a run that commits SES-006 and leaves README.md modified would still produce a clean `git status` only if it also committed README — worth an explicit check since the tool-owned index is a known footgun.

eval_feedback.overall: Two discriminating failures (reply length, OVERVIEW edit grounded in scaffolding) — the set is doing its job. Tighten the wording of the OVERVIEW expectation and add a cross-artifact consistency check.
